competencies.title: Essential project context
competencies.meaning: Keep the project meaning and judgment criteria AI needs in maintained context: business concepts, consequential decisions and their reasons, priorities, and exceptions that executable checks cannot fully express. Use lint, types, compiler checks, or CI for mechanically enforceable rules instead of repeating them as prose. Retain concise pointers to necessary setup and verification entry points; a command list is not a substitute for judgment context.
competencies.evidence: Read the authoritative context and its relevant references, then compare them with established project needs and decisions. Identify what a new executor needs to understand about the business, what remains a judgment call, and which repeated rules are already or could reasonably be enforced mechanically. Inspect applicable lint, type, compiler, or CI configuration when that distinction matters; do not assume a rule is enforced because the guide says so. Assess the content itself rather than its length, command count, or one executor's compliance. Use task records to establish which context is needed and whether a documented fact is accurate.
competencies.high: The maintained context contains the consequential business meaning, decision rationale, priorities, and exceptions needed for the work. Mechanically enforceable rules are handled through executable controls rather than repeated as instructions; the context focuses on what those controls cannot decide. Example: the guide explains who the service serves, what a consequential business term means, and why one outcome takes priority when requirements conflict, including the exception that changes that choice. It links to the setup and verification entry points, while import restrictions and formatting rules live in lint or CI configuration rather than a copied prose checklist.
competencies.medium: Useful project meaning is documented, but a consequential judgment criterion, decision reason, or exception is missing or ambiguous and must be reconstructed during work. The context may also rely on repeated prose rules for behavior that can reasonably be enforced mechanically. Example: the guide records the service's purpose and how to run its checks, but omits the agreed priority for a known business tradeoff; the person must explain that decision again. Most of the remaining instructions describe formatting and prohibited imports instead of supplying the missing rationale.
competencies.low: The context omits or misstates the project meaning needed for an established work opportunity, or consists of execution and style instructions without the judgment context that work requires. Example: a guide lists startup commands and coding conventions, but does not explain the relevant business concept or the reason behind an existing constraint; its only stated rule contradicts the confirmed project decision. The problem is the missing or misleading content, not the absence of a particular filename or an exhaustive repository description.
competencies.whyItHelps: Executable controls can catch a mechanically detectable violation without relying on AI remembering a sentence. Context remains valuable where those controls cannot decide what a business concept means, why a decision was made, or which outcome should take priority. Making those judgment calls and their failure modes explicit gives AI the information it cannot recover from syntax or a passing build, without burying it in repeated enforcement instructions.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when work depends on project meaning, an established decision, or a project-specific operating reference. Inspect the context needed for that work; do not demand documentation of routine facts AI can reliably discover or a separate paragraph for every check. Guidance delivery assesses whether the right material reaches the task, and guidance upkeep assesses its maintenance; neither substitutes for the quality of the content here.

sources.title: pstack — Encode Lessons in Structure
sources.note: Recommends encoding recurring corrections as lint, metadata, runtime checks, or scripts instead of more text. If a lesson requires judgment and cannot be encoded, it calls for a more prominent instruction and a failure-mode example; if the fix is structural, it calls for using that fix rather than adding another instruction. Adopted mechanism: reserve project context for necessary meaning and judgment while enforcing mechanically checkable rules in structure. This principle supports the distinction, not these assessment levels or a requirement to remove useful setup and verification references.

competencies.title: Context file organization
competencies.meaning: Give each AI executor a working route from shared entry guidance to the specialized information its task needs. Keep active guidance compatible across the tools actually used, and organize detail by a useful scope or task trigger. File length, file count, and automatic injection are not the assessed practice.
competencies.evidence: Follow the effective reading path for the observed client: launch directory, supported discovery settings and overrides, scope rules, explicit reads, references, and retrieved contents. Follow a relevant route into an action that uses the detail. When multiple clients participate, compare the instructions they actually receive. Inspect access or link failures and any repair before judging their effect; do not assume a nested file automatically loads in every client.
competencies.high: The active entry path reaches compatible shared rules and the needed specialized detail, and observed work applies that detail. The structure makes the relevant information available without making unrelated procedures a prerequisite to ordinary work. Example: a shared entry guide contains common directions and links to setup, release, and interface guidance by task. AI opens the relevant detail when needed, and the clients in use reach the same current common rules without loading unrelated procedures. A single small guide can also satisfy High when it supplies the relevant context effectively.
competencies.medium: The reading structure delivers useful guidance, but an observed delivery conflict or missing route requires the person's intervention to reach the correct source. Example: the common rules and task-specific pages exist, but one client's entry path still points to an older copy. The person supplies the current path before AI can use the right directions.
competencies.low: A relevant reading-path failure or conflicting delivery is observed, the executor continues without resolving it, and required guidance does not reach the work. Example: the entry guide links to a missing procedure, AI continues without the required instructions, and the delivered result omits the condition those instructions were meant to preserve. A broken link that is repaired before the guidance is needed does not establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: Information can constrain a decision only after the executor receives it. A useful entry map supplies the next document at the point where its details matter, while a shared authoritative rule avoids competing copies. On-demand retrieval can reduce irrelevant context, but adds navigation work; observed task use determines whether the chosen structure is effective.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an executor must receive maintained project guidance. Evaluate only tools and relevant paths used in the work; multiple tools or multiple files are optional. Do not impose modular files on an already usable small guide or reward splitting content into imports that all load together.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.note: The context-retrieval section describes lightweight references, retrieval when needed, and a hybrid of initial context and exploration. It also names navigation overhead. Adopt useful progressive disclosure, not a universal rule to minimize file length or retrieve everything lazily.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
sources.note: The discovery section specifies Codex's startup chain from project root to working directory, overrides, fallback names, and a combined size limit. This supports inspecting the effective client path rather than assuming every nested instruction file was injected.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project
sources.note: The loading, imports, and scoped-rule sections distinguish startup imports from conditional retrieval; AGENTS.md support also depends on client settings and version. Adopt client-aware delivery checks. Neither a shared filename nor an import alone proves relevant guidance influenced work.

competencies.title: Context maintenance
competencies.meaning: Keep active project guidance accurate as commands, locations, constraints, and decisions change. Use an applied maintenance mechanism that handles relevant updates as part of work, rather than depending on additional user intervention for every correction. Retire superseded directions and preserve valid guidance; do not generate documentation work without a real need.
competencies.evidence: Trace an actual project change or discovered guidance defect to the maintenance trigger, actor, saved authoritative revision, affected references, and check against the new project state. Inspect whether an established rule, workflow step, or automated check caused the update without additional user intervention for that task, and whether the repaired route or instruction was usable in actual work. Distinguish a completed update from a promise, and record later reuse only when observed.
competencies.high: An established workflow or automated check triggers the relevant upkeep without additional user intervention. AI corrects the authoritative guidance and affected routes, removes or clearly retires contradictory active directions, and checks the repaired content against actual project behavior. Example: a completed change moves a documented operation. The standing maintenance step updates its authoritative command and incoming links, retires the old directions, and checks the revised procedure against the changed project without additional user intervention. A standing instruction counts only when its upkeep behavior actually occurs; a separate scheduler or hook is optional.
competencies.medium: A useful, accurate repair is completed and checked, but the observed process depends on additional user intervention for that maintenance opportunity, or a partial repair demonstrably leaves competing guidance that requires intervention. Example: the person separately requests an update after an operation moves. AI corrects the documented command and relevant links, retires the old directions, and checks the revised procedure; the accurate repair still depends on that additional user intervention. This is effective upkeep with a person still initiating that recurring step.
competencies.low: A concrete change or exposed defect makes an active instruction wrong, a maintenance opportunity is observed, and the wrong direction remains prescribed or is reintroduced without correction. Example: the documented operation has moved and the obsolete directions have been identified, but the active guide still prescribes the old command and its links still lead to the removed location. A timestamp, an old document unrelated to the task, or lack of a later session does not establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: An accurate entry guide becomes misleading when its target moves or its procedure changes. Connecting upkeep to the relevant change closes that gap before the next executor relies on it. Retiring the old direction removes an avoidable choice between apparently valid procedures, while a real use of the revised instruction checks more than its wording.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an observed change or demonstrated defect creates a genuine guidance-maintenance need. Human approval of an unsettled policy decision is appropriate and does not prevent High. The AI can maintain confirmed facts automatically without inventing new policy.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.note: The repository-knowledge section describes documentation checks and a recurring agent that compares guidance with code behavior and proposes repairs. This supports applied automatic upkeep; it is one team's engineering account, not proof that a scheduled agent or any exact repository structure is necessary.

sources.title: Encode Lessons in Structure
sources.note: The skill recommends encoding recurring corrections in executable structure where possible, while retaining clearer instructions and failure examples for judgment calls. Adopt the distinction between repeatable mechanical upkeep and human policy judgment; do not turn every documentation edit into a new automation system.

boundaries: Assess maintained project guidance and its actual delivery here. Planning & Specs assesses the current task's goal, decisions, and constraints; the same fact appearing in both places does not justify duplicate credit for one act of clarification.

Memory & Knowledge assesses capture, reconciliation, and later use of reusable knowledge across conversations. A repair to a project's operating guide belongs here; storing the same repair through a memory mechanism does not create a second accomplishment.

Tool Integration assesses reusable executable procedures and direct service operation. A documented build command is context evidence; operating a reusable build procedure is a distinct behavior. Testing & Evals judges whether validation establishes product quality, while this dimension judges whether the guide describes a usable operation.

Security assesses authorization and sensitive-data protections that are actually applied. A documented prohibition can support instruction usability here, but its existence does not establish enforcement or safe execution.
Assess the observed information-to-action chain and its actor. Missing context, a failed reading route, contradictory content, and AI ignoring a rule already read are different causes.

example.notice: Illustrative guidance example, not evidence from this assessment.
example.summary: The project guide records the service's purpose and verification entry point, but leaves a consequential business priority for the person to explain again. Its shared entry links to task-specific detail, and the person separately prompts a checked update when an operation changes.
example.expanded: [pstack — Encode Lessons in Structure](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md) distinguishes executable enforcement from judgment that needs an explicit instruction and a failure-mode example. Here, the documented purpose is useful but the missing priority leaves the content incomplete. The working entry links support delivery, while the prompted, checked revision shows maintenance that still depends on a additional user intervention. Content, delivery, and upkeep are judged from their own evidence rather than from the presence of a guide alone.

competencies.title: Knowledge storage
competencies.meaning: Preserve information worth carrying into future conversations, with enough meaning, ownership, scope, and duration to distinguish a lasting preference from a temporary condition or a choice for one task.
competencies.evidence: Connect the original statement or adopted decision to the actual storage operation and inspect its saved result. Check the relevant user or project scope, any date or review condition that matters, and the rule that triggered capture. Identify whether AI captured the information through an existing procedure or the person had to request this particular save. A promise, enabled memory setting, or collection of files alone establishes neither capture nor accuracy.
competencies.high: A working reusable procedure causes AI to capture relevant knowledge without additional user intervention to save each item. The inspected entry preserves the intended meaning, scope, and lifetime, while temporary choices stay temporary. Example: a standing rule tells AI to save lasting project decisions. During ordinary work, the person settles a report format; AI stores that choice in project memory without an extra request to save it. A tone requested for one reply stays with that reply rather than becoming a permanent preference. A genuine decision about whether a preference should persist may still require the person's approval.
competencies.medium: An inspected save preserves usable knowledge with its intended scope and lifetime, but a reusable automatic capture procedure is not established; this includes a save requested for that particular item. A completed save that leaves a material scope or duration ambiguous also belongs here. Example: the person asks AI to remember a report format, and AI saves it with the correct project scope. The save is useful, but the record does not establish a procedure that captures later decisions without additional user intervention. Credit the confirmed save without claiming that additional user interventions are always necessary.
competencies.low: Observed capture leaves knowledge materially wrong or contrary to an explicit scope or duration, and the mismatch remains unresolved in the saved result. Example: the person requests a casual tone for one reply, but AI saves it as the default for all future customer replies and leaves that incorrect entry active. This is a demonstrated incorrect memory, rather than an assumption based on missing write records.
competencies.whyItHelps: Useful persistence carries the decision the person meant to preserve into the situations that need it. Scope and lifetime prevent a local exception from becoming an unrelated default. Automatic capture removes the recurring need to turn ordinary decisions into separate memory-management requests.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when work introduces reusable preferences, corrections, decisions, or facts worth retaining. A confirmed usable save remains Medium when only the reusable trigger required for High is unverified; report that limit without inventing manual dependence. Appropriate delegation to AI or native memory qualifies; the person need not choose a database, write a file, or restate facts AI can investigate.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project — Auto memory
sources.note: Describes AI-written notes derived from preferences and corrections, project-specific storage, and selecting information useful in future conversations. This supports selective automatic capture; it does not establish that any particular person's memory is accurate.

sources.title: Memory overview — Long-term memory and Writing memories
sources.note: Distinguishes thread state from memory across conversations, scopes records through namespaces, and describes runtime or background writes. These mechanisms support choosing an appropriate persistence boundary without requiring a particular storage product.

competencies.title: Knowledge maintenance
competencies.meaning: Review retained knowledge when its facts, conditions, or scope may have changed; preserve what remains valid and reconcile corrections, duplicates, conflicts, and expired entries into a clear active answer.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the prior entries, the change or confirmation that prompted review, the actual maintenance operation, and the resulting active knowledge. Check whether a reusable trigger handled the event without additional user intervention for maintenance. Replacement, merging, retirement, explicit precedence, and deliberate retention can all be appropriate. If a management rule was repaired, inspect an actual subsequent operation before claiming that the revised rule works.
competencies.high: An existing procedure responds to a relevant correction, changed condition, or review trigger and AI reconciles the affected knowledge without requiring the person to direct routine cleanup. The resulting active entries give a coherent answer and preserve unrelated valid facts. Example: the person changes a previously saved project decision. The established update procedure causes AI to replace the old active entry, preserve useful history separately, and check for conflicting notes without an extra instruction to clean up memory. Review may confirm an entry is still valid; High does not require an edit or an invented conflict.
competencies.medium: An inspected review or correction produces a coherent, current active memory, but a reusable procedure that initiates routine upkeep is not established; this includes a correction specifically requested by the person. An actual maintenance operation that leaves a material conflict unresolved also belongs here. Example: the person specifically asks AI to replace an outdated memory entry. AI makes an accurate correction, but the record does not establish how later changes will trigger upkeep without additional user intervention. Credit the completed reconciliation without asserting that every correction needs a separate request.
competencies.low: A known false, superseded, or expired entry remains prescribed after its status is established and the maintenance action is completed without resolving it. Example: the person confirms that an old project rule no longer applies. AI claims to update memory, but the saved active entry still tells later work to follow that old rule. Missing review records alone do not demonstrate this behavior.
competencies.whyItHelps: A memory can be faithfully retrieved and still be wrong because its facts have changed. Reconciliation makes the active answer current and reduces arbitrary choices between conflicting entries. Event-based upkeep carries corrections forward without making the person repeatedly supervise storage housekeeping.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when retained knowledge is reviewed or a relevant change, conflict, duplicate, expiry, or confirmation creates a maintenance opportunity. A confirmed completed correction remains Medium when only the reusable upkeep trigger required for High is unverified. Automatic means a demonstrated reusable procedure operates when needed; it does not require a background service, fixed schedule, constant rewriting, or automatic resolution of a genuine human decision.

sources.title: Memory overview — Semantic memory
sources.note: Explains updating an existing profile and the need to update or delete items in memory collections. It identifies over-insertion and over-updating as management difficulties, supporting inspection of the resulting active set rather than credit for appending another note.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project — How it works
sources.note: Describes an index with detailed topic files, on-demand reads, and maintenance that merges or drops stale entries. Successful writes can exceed what the next conversation loads, so storage success alone does not prove maintained knowledge is usable.

competencies.title: Knowledge reuse
competencies.meaning: Use the relevant active knowledge to make a correct choice in a separate later conversation, respecting its scope, corrections, and retirement instead of making the person supply it again.
competencies.evidence: Trace a retained fact into a later independent conversation where it affects the requested work, or trace a later choice back to the active memory that informed it. Inspect the actual answer, implementation, or operation and its relevant result. Establish which version applied at that time and whether the person restated the fact or reminded AI to consult memory. An explicit read is unnecessary when injected knowledge is demonstrably used; reading, injection, or a claim of remembering is insufficient by itself.
competencies.high: Later work uses the applicable active knowledge correctly without additional user intervention to consult memory or a repetition of the saved fact. The produced result confirms that the knowledge guided the work. Example: an earlier conversation saves the project's report format, and a standing startup instruction retrieves relevant memory. In a new conversation, the person requests a report without repeating the format or asking AI to consult memory. AI receives the saved decision through startup or retrieval and produces the report in that format. A native retrieval feature or an established startup procedure can supply the memory. Installation, a loaded note, or repeating the decision in a progress message earns no credit without the actual choice and result.
competencies.medium: The later result ultimately applies the retained knowledge, but the person has to repeat it or explicitly redirect AI to the memory before it governs the work. Example: AI starts a later report in the wrong format. The person points it to the saved decision, and AI then uses the correct format in the delivered report. The correction succeeds, while the person still carries the recall burden.
competencies.low: Later work demonstrably uses an inapplicable, retired, or contradicted memory, or disregards an available applicable memory, and the resulting mismatch remains unresolved. Example: the saved report format is current and relevant to a later request, but AI delivers the retired format and leaves the mismatch unresolved. A later correction must be included when judging the final behavior; lack of a later record is never this failure.
competencies.whyItHelps: Persistence becomes useful when it changes the work that reaches the person. Examining a later result separates effective recall from storage and prompt loading, while respecting scope prevents an accurate fact about one project from distorting another.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when a separate later conversation presents an opportunity to use retained knowledge. A correction in the original conversation establishes neither persistence nor later application.

sources.title: pstack — Recall (skills/recall/SKILL.md)
sources.note: Reconstructs relevant goals, decisions, and corrections before work resumes, limits retrieval to the intended workspace and topic, and checks findings against live state. This supports relevant, current recall; invoking the skill alone does not prove that its findings changed the work.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents — Structured note-taking
sources.note: Describes agents persisting notes outside the context window and reading them after resets to continue work. The adopted mechanism is continuity through notes that guide subsequent actions, rather than accumulating an archive.

boundaries: Assess the person's retained working knowledge here, separately from a memory feature they build for their product. No memory product, store count, archive size, or particular file format is required.

Context Engineering covers maintained project operating guidance and how relevant material reaches the task. This dimension covers preferences, corrections, decisions, and facts retained over conversations, their currency, and their actual use. Do not score one project-guide repair again as memory maintenance.

Tool Integration covers executable procedures; Task Mapping and Feedback Loops cover arrangement and execution decisions; Testing & Evals covers verification quality. Saving those same procedures is not additional memory credit. Distinct retained knowledge may be assessed when its own lifecycle is evidenced.

Capture, reconciliation, and later application require different connected evidence. Do not collapse failures to save, retrieve, scope, update, and follow retrieved knowledge into one presumed memory failure.

For capture and reconciliation, High requires a working reusable automatic procedure and an observed correct operation. Standing instructions carried out by AI can qualify; an instruction alone cannot. Correct on-demand management is Medium. Human approval of an unresolved preference or decision does not by itself reduce the level.

Account for later repairs and identify the person, AI, or storage mechanism responsible. Do not invent a conflict, change, later task, or incident to create evidence. Apply the shared qualitative judgment policy.

example.notice: Illustrative output example, not evidence from this assessment.
example.summary: AI saved the project's report format under an existing memory rule, keeping a one-reply tone exception out of lasting preferences. In a later conversation, AI received that saved format through the startup procedure and used it in the delivered report without additional user intervention.
example.expanded: The memory sources connect useful storage to accurate boundaries and later application. In this example, the saved entry records what should persist and where it applies. The later conversation supplies the separate reuse evidence: AI receives the relevant entry through the existing startup route and the report follows it, even though the person did not repeat the decision or request a memory lookup. A note merely appearing in the context would not establish that final connection.

competencies.title: Tool connections
competencies.meaning: Use a suitable connection to carry out the service work a task actually needs, and carry the returned records or operation result through to the requested deliverable.
competencies.evidence: Follow the request into the chosen CLI, API, MCP tool, or equivalent connection. Inspect the account, project, record identifiers, inputs, execution result, and resulting deliverable or service state. Determine whether returned information was used in the next necessary action. A listed connection, capability lookup, successful handshake, or completion message alone does not establish completed service work.
competencies.high: The agent performs the required authorized service operations against the correct target and uses the returned information to finish the requested work; the inspected result supports that completion. Example: AI uses connected tools to read the records needed for a report, obtains missing items through the same connections, and returns a report that matches those records. A one-off request can meet High through its own completed operations.
competencies.medium: The connection performs a useful part of the task, but an observed, avoidable handoff leaves the person to transfer information or perform a routine operation the available tool could handle. Example: AI reads record identifiers through a working connection, but asks the person to copy the associated details even though its connected tool can retrieve them. The report is finished only after that manual transfer.
competencies.low: An available, authorized operation needed for the task is omitted or executed against the wrong target, and the observed work remains incorrect or is completed manually because that omission is left unresolved. Example: AI reads the test account instead of the required live account, reports the wrong record status, and leaves that claim unchanged after the account mismatch is shown. Missing execution logs alone cannot establish Low.
competencies.whyItHelps: The connection gives the agent access to the records and actions needed to finish the request. Using the returned identifiers and state removes routine copying by the person and prevents a successful tool response from being mistaken for completion of a different task.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when the task needs service records or actions that can appropriately be handled through an available connection. Appropriate human approval is compatible with High; the person need not write the integration or supply details the agent can investigate.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
sources.note: Recommends task-focused tools, useful returned context, explicit input/output contracts, and verifiable outcomes. The adopted mechanism is a connected operation whose returned data supports completing the user's actual task, rather than a bonus for the number of tools.

sources.title: Tools — Model Context Protocol
sources.note: Defines tool discovery separately from invocation and describes execution errors returned with isError: true. This supports inspecting the actual operation result instead of treating any response or successful connection as completed work.

competencies.title: Reusable skills
competencies.meaning: Put recurring operational knowledge into a runnable skill, command, script, or configured tool procedure that can handle another relevant task with new inputs.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the retained procedure and the operational resources it invokes, including how it obtains task inputs, selects the environment, performs actions, and produces the needed output. Connect that version to an independent later task and its inspected result. Record whether the person named the procedure, a standing route selected it, or the person had to reconstruct its steps. Calls repeated within one run are not independent reuse.
competencies.high: A retained procedure runs on a later relevant task with changed task inputs and produces the intended inspected output without the person explaining its operating sequence again. The agent can discover routine inputs from the documented sources. Example: a saved skill gathers the required inputs, runs its processing steps, and returns a checked report. On a later request it accepts the new date range and repeats the work without the person explaining the sequence again. Naming the skill and correct automatic selection can both establish reuse.
competencies.medium: The saved procedure is used on a later task and contributes useful execution, but a demonstrated omission still makes the person restate an operational step before the result is usable. Example: a reused skill completes the main calculation, but omits the export step. The person must explain that step again before receiving a usable report.
competencies.low: An attempted reuse shows that the retained procedure cannot perform its claimed recurring work, and the person must rebuild the operational sequence or do the work manually while the deficiency remains. Example: invoking the saved skill only lists available tools; it does not perform the promised task. The person has to reconstruct the full sequence during the attempted reuse.
competencies.whyItHelps: A working retained procedure carries the operating sequence between tasks, so a new request can focus on the new period or desired result. Bundled operations and clear input sources make reuse possible without turning the person into the tool's instruction manual.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when recurring work or a concrete later-use opportunity is observed. Existing third-party procedures and procedures written by AI qualify when the person adopts and actually uses them.

sources.title: Specification — Agent Skills
sources.note: Separates discovery metadata, loaded instructions, and optional executable resources; recommends operational steps, input/output examples, and documented script dependencies. The rubric adopts the runnable instruction/resource package while requiring observed reuse beyond format validity.

sources.title: Writing Skills
sources.note: Distinguishes reusable skills from a narrative of one solved task and checks technique skills through application to a new scenario. This supports requiring another actual use rather than crediting a saved retrospective as a reusable procedure.

competencies.title: Tool maintenance
competencies.meaning: Keep the saved operational mechanism aligned with changed services, environments, or task requirements, and confirm that the affected operation still works.
competencies.evidence: Trace an actual change or failure to the diagnosis, the retained configuration or procedure version, an invocation of the affected path, and the inspected output. Distinguish an effective saved repair from a conversation-only workaround. Where upkeep recurs, inspect the standing instruction, event, or check that brings it into relevant tasks and whether that route is actually applied.
competencies.high: The observed maintenance need leads to a targeted saved repair, followed by a real invocation showing that the affected behavior now meets the need. When maintenance recurs, an applied standing route handles routine detection and repair without requiring the person to repeat the maintenance checklist. Example: a service changes the data its tool returns. The existing check detects the change, AI updates the saved skill's mapping and report step, and a real run confirms that the revised tool combination works without additional user intervention to repeat the maintenance steps. A checked existing mechanism that already handles the change may be retained.
competencies.medium: The task reaches a corrected result, but the repair remains partly in the conversation or requires a demonstrated manual patch, leaving the saved mechanism incomplete. Example: AI fixes the data-reading step but leaves the saved report step outdated. The person supplies the missing adjustment, and AI corrects only the current output without saving the complete repair.
competencies.low: A known relevant defect or change is left in the active mechanism, and an inspected affected invocation repeats its incorrect behavior without correction. Example: a known data mismatch remains in a frequently used skill. The next run repeats the same incorrect report because the saved tool combination was not corrected.
competencies.whyItHelps: Saving the repair changes what the next invocation will do. Exercising the exact affected path reveals whether the correction reaches the delivered output, while an applied upkeep route prevents the same operational repair from becoming a recurring additional user intervention for the person.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when an actual maintenance need or an observed scheduled suitability check occurs. Approval of a consequential change remains a legitimate human decision; automated upkeep need not expand access or bypass that decision.

sources.title: Automate me
sources.note: Its update path reuses the existing skill, considers evidence since its last edit, preserves uncontradicted sections, and revises changed rules in place. The adopted mechanism is targeted maintenance of retained instructions; its personal-mode evaluation advice is not treated as proof of executable workflow behavior.

sources.title: Writing Skills
sources.note: Recommends identifying the specific failure, changing the guidance to address it, and checking application again. The rubric adopts that observed failure-to-repair-to-use connection, without importing its mandatory TDD or subagent workflow as a scoring condition.

competencies.title: Skill sharing
competencies.meaning: Transfer a working procedure to another intended user in a form that can operate with that user's environment and inputs.
competencies.evidence: Inspect the version already used in the person's own work, the package or shared files, supporting scripts, setup and configuration directions, and a concrete invocation and expected output. Follow a recipient's run or a fresh-environment rehearsal through those directions. Look for hidden local paths, omitted helpers, and setup knowledge that the author has to supply separately. Publicity and repository stars are not usability evidence.
competencies.high: The provided package includes the needed operational resources and directions, and a recipient or fresh-environment rehearsal reaches the intended output using those resources and its own configuration without undocumented author-local steps. Example: a shared skill includes its helper files, setup directions, and required configuration. Another person, or a fresh-environment rehearsal, uses their own configuration and obtains the documented result without extra setup instructions from the author. The author or AI may perform the rehearsal.
competencies.medium: The shared procedure can produce its intended output, but the observed setup or invocation still depends on avoidable guidance outside the package. Example: another person can run the shared skill only after the author separately explains where a required configuration file belongs; that instruction is still missing from the package.
competencies.low: An inspected portability defect prevents the offered package from performing the promised procedure, and the defect remains unresolved. Example: the shared skill depends on a helper available only on the author's computer, so it fails for the recipient and no usable replacement is supplied.
competencies.whyItHelps: A usable package transfers the operating capability together with its environment requirements. Running it from the recipient's starting point exposes dependencies hidden by the author's machine and shows whether the shared instructions actually lead to the intended result.
competencies.applicability: Applicable only when sharing or transfer is part of the observed work. A private personal procedure does not need to be published. Private team distribution qualifies, and neither audience size nor popularity changes the behavioral level.

sources.title: Specification — Agent Skills
sources.note: Describes environment compatibility information, supporting resources, relative file references, and self-contained scripts or explicit dependencies. These support portable packaging; the fresh-environment demonstration is this rubric's evidence requirement, not a claim made by format validation.

sources.title: Writing Skills
sources.note: Recommends runnable examples and testing whether a user can find and apply a reference, including gaps in common use cases. This supports checking the receiving user's actual path through shared operating material.

boundaries: Assess tools the person adopts for their own work. Building or demonstrating an integration for customers does not establish personal workflow use.

Direct service work concerns completed tool-mediated operations; reusable executable procedures concern carrying an operating sequence to a later task. Neither requires a particular tool type, tool count, custom implementation, or fixed elapsed period.

Context Engineering owns project guidance, its reading route, and guide upkeep. Tool Integration owns saved operational mechanisms that actually execute work, including their configuration and maintenance. A project command mentioned in a guide is not automatically a reusable executed procedure.

Task Mapping owns work assignments, dependencies, handoffs, and integration. Feedback Loops owns how returned observations decide a retry, correction, stop, or escalation. Testing & Evals owns what checks establish about the produced result; inspecting a tool result here establishes that the tool operation or repair took effect, without awarding separate verification coverage.

Memory & Knowledge owns the lifecycle of remembered facts and decisions. Saving this same procedure is not a second memory-management action. Security owns authorization and information boundaries; necessary human approval does not reduce tool-integration credit.
Neither missing records nor absence of a need to create, repair, automate, or share a tool establishes Low.

competencies.title: Task breakdown
competencies.meaning: Shape the necessary work into bounded assignments with an inspectable result and a meaningful completion condition. Choose boundaries that cover the request without leaving gaps or duplicating responsibility. One coherent assignment is enough for a small task.
competencies.evidence: Follow the request and the arrangement actually used into assignment briefs, task records, returned artifacts, and per-part checks. Identify what each part owns, what it must return, and how its executor judged that result. Credit prior instructions or an AI-proposed division the person adopts when execution applies them; a diagram, role name, or unused plan is insufficient.
competencies.high: The applied units cover the necessary deliverables, have distinct responsibilities, and return results that are examined against their own completion conditions. Example: a report request is divided into data collection and report preparation. Each part has a clear owner, an output, and a check for completion; together they cover the requested report. A label correction remains one assignment and its rendered replacement is checked.
competencies.medium: The executed assignments have useful boundaries and concrete returns, but an observed ambiguity leaves part of completion to guesswork. Example: data collection and report preparation have separate outputs, but the handling of invalid records remains undecided. The person assembling the report must settle that gap.
competencies.low: The actual division leaves a required deliverable uncovered or gives overlapping ownership without a useful purpose, and that structural gap causes missing or duplicated work that remains unresolved. Example: two assignments both rewrite the same data-reading step, while neither owns the requested report. The work ends with overlapping changes and a missing deliverable.
competencies.whyItHelps: A bounded result gives the executor a target and lets another step judge what is ready. Relating all units to the request exposes omitted work; distinguishing their responsibilities prevents two returns from being mistaken for coverage of two different needs.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when work needs an execution scope and completion condition, including a small task kept whole. Do not require the person to supply facts AI can inspect, write implementation details, or divide work personally.

sources.title: Planning and Task Breakdown — skills/planning-and-task-breakdown/SKILL.md
sources.note: Recommends verifiable task results, acceptance criteria, verification steps, and dependencies; it also excludes obvious small changes from a separate planning exercise. These mechanisms support checkable boundaries, without adopting its file-count or checkpoint quotas.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.note: Describes delegation briefs with an objective, expected format, tools and sources, and boundaries, and reports duplicate work and gaps from vague briefs. The adopted mechanism is explicit responsibility and a usable return, not a required number of agents.

competencies.title: Result integration
competencies.meaning: Carry the actual output of one part to the part that needs it, respect prerequisite order, and assemble a result whose connected assumptions agree. Separate completion claims must resolve into the requested combined result.
competencies.evidence: Trace the relevant producer artifact or revision into its consumer's reads, input, or execution. Inspect how shared definitions were settled, who assembled the returns, and the observed comparison at their connection: fields, units, versions, responsibilities, or coverage. Then connect that assembled artifact to the requested outcome. A worker saying 'done' or a generic check passing does not prove this chain.
competencies.high: The dependent part uses the completed prerequisite actually produced, and observed integration confirms that the returns fit and satisfy the combined request. Accessible intermediate outputs reach their consumers through the workflow without repeated human copying. Example: the report step uses the records returned by the collection step. Their field names and units agree, and a check of the assembled report confirms that the parts work together.
competencies.medium: Actual outputs reach the next part and are assembled, but a known unperformed boundary check or repeated manual relay leaves a connection unestablished. Example: the collection and report changes are assembled, but the recorded check uses a separately typed sample instead of the actual returned records. The connection between the two parts remains unverified.
competencies.low: An observed missing, stale, or incompatible handoff prevents the parts from fitting, yet separate completion reports are accepted as the combined result without reconciliation. Example: the collection step returns one field name while the report expects another. Both parts are marked complete, but their mismatch remains in the delivered result.
competencies.whyItHelps: A result can be correct in isolation and unusable to its consumer. Following the exact return across the boundary reveals absent or stale inputs, while comparison after assembly exposes disagreements that isolated completion reports cannot settle.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when outputs depend on or must be assembled with other outputs, whether one executor or several perform the work. A failure wholly inside a correctly connected part is not automatically a mapping failure.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.note: Distinguishes sequential output-to-input chains from independent parallel sections and describes an orchestrator synthesizing worker returns. These patterns support tracing real dependencies and aggregation; the rubric additionally requires observed fit with the person's requested result.

sources.title: Swarm — skills/swarm/SKILL.md
sources.note: Requires a defined final artifact and completion condition, self-contained briefs, inspection of terminal results, and coverage of required slices before consolidation. The adopted mechanism is checking returns against their briefs and exposing missing contributions instead of treating them as success.

competencies.title: Work assignment
competencies.meaning: Match responsibility, context, access, and execution order to the actual work. Use one executor, sequential parts, or concurrent parts when that arrangement permits useful work without conflicting ownership or unsupported assumptions.
competencies.evidence: Compare each assignment's requirements with the context, tools, access, and writable scope its executor actually receives. Inspect dependencies and concurrent activity for shared-state conflicts, duplicated effort, and waiting caused by missing prerequisites. Distinguish deliberate independent review or alternative attempts from accidental overlap. Count the observed fit, not the number of workers or tool calls.
competencies.high: Execution demonstrates that assignments have the required capabilities and that ownership and ordering let their results fit. Dependent work waits for the shared prerequisite; concurrent work has independent scope or an explicit comparison purpose. Example: one owner settles the shared data definition before dependent work starts. Independent work proceeds separately, and the returned parts fit that definition. The same arrangement can run sequentially in one session.
competencies.medium: The arrangement enables useful progress but reveals a preventable capability or ownership mismatch that requires an extra coordination step. Example: the report assignment has a useful scope but receives an outdated input definition. An additional coordination step supplies the current definition before the work can finish. The mismatch is corrected rather than repeatedly imposed.
competencies.low: The arrangement demonstrably blocks assigned work or creates conflicting contributions and continues despite that evidence. Example: two workers overwrite the same shared definition and produce incompatible results, yet the work continues without assigning ownership or resolving the dependency.
competencies.whyItHelps: An executor cannot complete work that requires unavailable inputs or access. Settling shared prerequisites and ownership lets useful independent work proceed while avoiding results built on incompatible assumptions. A suitable single-session sequence can achieve this without coordination overhead.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when choosing who or which step does work, including keeping a small or tightly coupled task with one executor. No multiple-agent, concurrency, or specialization requirement applies. Model price, reasoning effort, and total resource tradeoffs belong primarily to Efficiency & Cost.

sources.title: Dispatching Parallel Agents — skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md
sources.note: Uses parallel investigations for independent domains, warns against shared state and interfering edits, and requires checking that returned fixes do not conflict. This supports the independence and ownership test; its worker-count examples are not scoring requirements.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.note: Recommends beginning with the simplest effective arrangement and adding complexity when useful. This supports crediting a coherent single executor and choosing dependency chains or parallel sections according to the work.

competencies.title: Reusable workflows
competencies.meaning: Keep task boundaries and handoffs useful as work changes, and carry a demonstrated arrangement into comparable later work. Preserve a working structure or revise a structural cause using execution evidence, instead of reconstructing the same assignments each time.
competencies.evidence: Compare the applied arrangement across a relevant change or independent matching tasks. Trace observed gaps, collisions, waiting, or successful connections to retained or revised ownership, task size, order, and handoffs. For recurring work, inspect whether an existing entry point retrieves and applies the current structure without the person restating it, and whether later outputs demonstrate its fit. A stored procedure alone is insufficient.
competencies.high: The active structure is checked against changed or comparable work; any affected responsibility and handoff are kept aligned before dependent work uses them, and subsequent returns demonstrate that the connections work. For recurring work, an ordinary request retrieves and applies the demonstrated structure without additional user intervention to rebuild its assignments. Example: a later request reuses a saved task plan. When the input format changes, the plan's responsibilities and handoffs are updated together before dependent work uses them. Inspected connections that still fit can remain unchanged.
competencies.medium: Continuing or later work uses a workable structure, but its upkeep or reuse still depends on the person reconstructing coordination that the workflow could carry forward. Example: a later task reuses the same division successfully only after the person repeats who owns each part and how results should be handed over. The saved plan still contains the old arrangement. The result works, while maintained reuse remains incomplete.
competencies.low: Known structural changes or recurring coordination failures are left out of the actual arrangement, causing the same gap again without correction. Example: earlier runs exposed a dependency that must finish before report work starts. The next comparable run repeats the old order and again builds the report from an obsolete input definition.
competencies.whyItHelps: Reuse preserves decisions that already made the parts work together. Keeping the active structure aligned with changed responsibilities prevents an old handoff from silently governing new work. Observing subsequent execution distinguishes an effective structural repair from an instruction that was merely saved.
competencies.applicability: Applicable when changed responsibilities or dependencies require upkeep, or when a later comparable task offers reuse. Human approval of a real responsibility or outcome decision is compatible with High. Do not require new incidents, a changed arrangement, or more agents; retaining or simplifying a verified working arrangement qualifies.

sources.title: Encode Lessons in Structure — skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md
sources.note: Recommends encoding repeated corrections in an executable or structural mechanism, while leaving judgment-dependent lessons as clearer guidance with an example. This supports a reusable assignment mechanism without automating personal judgment. Actual later application and maintained handoffs are rubric requirements, not claimed validation from this source.

boundaries: Task Mapping assesses the applied division, ownership, dependencies, transfer of outputs, and assembly of the requested result. Planning establishes the intended outcome and decisions; a plan becomes mapping evidence only when its arrangement guides actual work.

The integration observation here asks whether the assigned parts and their actual returns fit together. Testing & Evals assesses what a check proves about user behavior or AI output quality. Feedback Loops assesses the next action taken from a returned result, such as retrying, stopping, or escalating. A failure inside a correctly assigned part does not by itself establish a mapping failure.

The maintained/reused structure row concerns whether current responsibilities and handoffs govern later work. Tool Integration assesses making the procedure executable, connected, maintained, and shareable. Saving the same procedure is not a second Memory & Knowledge practice unless a distinct fact or decision lifecycle is established.

Credit the arrangement the person requests or adopts, including prior instructions that are actually applied. Attribute an AI-designed division to AI rather than inventing human design work. Human Steering examines the person's own decisions about proposals, corrections, and earlier assumptions; an automated coordinator's choice does not establish those decisions.

No agent count, parallel execution, tool count, written code by the person, added orchestration layer, or structural revision is required. A single executor, a direct small task, intentional independent review, and retaining a working arrangement can all be appropriate.

example.expanded: The task-planning sources support clear ownership, usable returned work, and explicit dependencies.
